data.title: Build the bootstrap core
data.description:
The `bootstrap` binary needs a library that holds its decisions, with the CLI and server as thin layers over it. This leaf makes that library. Everything else in the binary builds on it.

What exists when it's done: a Go module at the repo root using only the standard library, with cgo off. `bootstrap`, `detect`, `tools` and `screens` work, printing terse rows by default and a stable shape with `--json`, and none of them needs a session. The catalog of tools lives in `catalog/tools.json`, embedded in the binary and readable as a raw file, so the chat fallback in `SETUP.md` can use the same facts when the binary can't run. The screens from the prototype are defined in Go as closed lists, each producing the description the page draws, including the swap of `{app}` and `{ai}` for Claude Code or OpenCode. Progress is calculated from the screen, the tool and the user's choices; callers never pass a percentage.

Already decided (project/2026-11-05-setup-link-plan.md, "The interface", and project/2026-11-05-bootstrap-binary-plan.md): Go; all copy in the binary; very few words at a 6th-grade reading level; the tool is called Jobs in anything a person reads. Detect Apple's tools by `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/git`, never `xcode-select -p` or `command -v git`, because `/usr/bin/git` is a stub until they're installed. Copy each screen's words from the `SCREENS` object in project/2026-11-05-setup-page-mock/prototype/template.html.

Seams: the leaf "Build the server and CLI" consumes this; the leaf "Port the page" draws the description. Check in one JSON sample per screen, generated and compared by a Go test, because JavaScript can't import a Go struct and the page is the other side of that seam.

Out of scope: the server, the page and signing. The "needs a newer Mac" screen is dropped, since an arm64 binary can't start on an Intel Mac. The prototype's study bar and fake waits aren't part of the product.

The house CLI rules bind this leaf and the server leaf: read project/agents/cli-design.md. They cover the primer, one shape per verb, the shared exit codes, errors that name the next command, and tests that drive the binary.

The agent's call: exact field names and package layout, keeping files small.

data.title: Build the server and CLI
data.description:
This is how the agent and the page talk. An agent runs short commands and a person clicks in a browser, and this leaf connects the two without opening anything to the rest of the machine.

What exists when it's done: `bootstrap serve --agent <name>` detaches itself, binds to 127.0.0.1 on a free port, opens the browser with `/usr/bin/open`, and reports the URL and whether the browser opened. The session is an append-only JSONL log readable only by its owner. `show` appends to it, the page's answers land in it, `wait` and `status` read it, and `stop` ends the session. The commands never talk to the server. The server tails the log, sends new screens to the page over Server-Sent Events, and appends the answers it receives. `wait answer|clt|brew` returns what it waited for, or exits 3 with "still waiting, run wait again". Answers to an earlier screen are never returned.

Already decided (project/2026-11-05-setup-link-plan.md): bind to loopback, require a random token on the page's requests, check Host and Origin, exit after the agent is gone. Standard library only. From project/2026-11-05-bootstrap-binary-plan.md: every command renews a time allowance, three minutes by default or longer with `show --expect`. Past it while the agent is working, the page shows the lost screen, "Whoops! We lost your {app} session. Open it back up and type “continue”." (Ben's wording). While the page waits on the user nothing changes until they click, when the click is saved and the lost screen appears if no agent has checked recently. The next command from any session brings the page back. The server keeps running while the tab is open, up to about an hour, then exits, and `serve` starts fresh from the same log. A second `serve` reuses a live session. A typed project name must be a safe folder name, because an agent will use it in commands. The house CLI rules bind this leaf: project/agents/cli-design.md.

Seams: the library from "Build the bootstrap core" holds the decisions; this layer stays thin. The page is another leaf, so test with plain HTTP clients.

Open, the agent's call: where bootstrap's folder lives, which pro mode's preferences file (t5FAqu) will share. Open for the trial, so make them easy to change: the default `wait` timeout, and the exact lost-screen line.

Risks: `serve` must fail with clear JSON rather than hang when it can't bind or open a browser, because that failure is what sends the agent to the chat fallback. A sandboxed agent can't bind a port or run `open`, and that should read as a normal fallback. A machine sleeping through an allowance shouldn't count as the agent leaving, or at least should recover when it wakes.

Already decided (Ben, 2026-11-05; project/2026-11-05-setup-link-plan.md, "The interface"): silk threads in linear light, blue through cyan to green with progress, relaxing to the starting form. No hard cuts: what leaves and what arrives share one 1.4s S-curve, and the object never moves. Fast while working, slow while waiting. Grand Medium for titles and Regular for buttons, subset to Latin. Three.js r128, the fonts and the images are embedded, with no CDN. Copy the shaders and timing constants from project/2026-11-05-setup-page-mock/prototype/template.html rather than rewriting them.

Keep the prototype's reduced-motion handling, and its eight-bit path for when the float buffer isn't available. Keep Three.js's license with the vendored copy. Tool names link to their repos.

data.text: Research, 2026-11-05, from code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md and mobile.md: Remote Control works on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise, not Free and not with an API key. Team and Enterprise need an Owner to turn it on in claude.ai admin settings (claude-code). It isn't available through Bedrock, Google Cloud, Foundry, a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or an enterprise gateway. On the Mac: signed in with a claude.ai account (/login), and the claude process must keep running; closing the terminal takes it offline. If the Mac sleeps, it reconnects when the Mac wakes; the docs don't mention keep-awake settings. Start it with `/remote-control` in a session, `claude --remote-control`, or `claude remote-control`. Then, on the phone, open the Claude app with the same account, tap Code and pick the session (or use the URL or QR code). Bypass permissions can't be chosen from the app. The docs give no minimum version. There's no official OpenCode equivalent (only third-party apps). For SETUP.md: offer it only to Pro and above with a claude.ai login, and say the Mac must stay on with the terminal open.

data.title: Check each install step runs from the detached server
data.description:
Why: the server will run every install itself, as a detached background process started by the agent's shell. Some steps may need a terminal or a GUI session, and the installer leaf builds differently for each step that can't run detached: that step becomes a handoff to the agent.

The question, per step: run from a process started the way `bootstrap serve` starts its server (re-launched in the background, no terminal), does it work? The steps: `xcode-select --install` and raising Apple's window with `open -a`; downloading Homebrew's latest `.pkg` from its GitHub releases, checking its signer (927JGANW46) and notarization, and opening it; `brew trust bensyverson/tap` and `brew install` by full path; `agents init`, `job init`, `git init`; and `gh auth login --hostname github.com --web --git-protocol https --skip-ssh-key`, reading the one-time code from its output and getting past its "Press Enter" prompt with no terminal.

Where: a fresh Tart clone on the Mini (`tart clone ghcr.io/cirruslabs/macos-tahoe-vanilla:latest <name>`, then `spctl --global-enable` and remove `/etc/sudoers.d/admin-nopasswd`); project/2026-11-05-handoff-vm.md has the access details. Run the steps from a small throwaway Go program or a `nohup`/`setsid`-style launch that matches how the server detaches. Its code is disposable. Ben clicks Apple's and Homebrew's windows. A GitHub sign-in needs an account: ask Ben which one to use, and never record its token.

Findings go in project/2026-11-05-vm-run-findings.md as a new section, or a new dated doc, and as a note on the installer leaf.

data.description:

What: a click acknowledges itself within a frame. The answered screen moves into a waiting state, following the no-hard-cuts rule (every change animates on the shared 1.4s S-curve, and the object never moves; see "The interface" in project/2026-11-05-setup-link-plan.md), and it holds until the next screen arrives. When a session ends on a screen that isn't settled, the server shows an internal end screen, like `lost`, with Ben's words: title "That's all for now.", line "You can close this and go back to {app}." It settles the blob.

data.title: Build the flow core
data.description:
Why: the setup order moves from SETUP.md's prose into code the server runs, so it can't be skipped or reordered and can be tested. This is the library the verbs and installers plug into.

What: a new package, internal/flow. The setup is a list of steps as data, each with a check (already done?), an act, the screens it shows, and the answers it needs from the page. A step's outcome is done, skipped, needs the person (a page screen), or a handoff to the agent with a reason, the evidence and the ways forward. Every outside command goes through a `Runner` interface, so tests use a fake and no test touches the Mac. The flow writes every step, event and handoff to the session log, as `show` does today, so `status` and `wait` read it with no server connection.

The order is in project/2026-11-05-server-driven-flow.md, "What the server does": Apple's tools, Homebrew, tools, then the project part (name and folder, Git, GitHub, stage questions, agents init, local/, job init), machine settings, phone, done. The tools come from the person's picks on the list screen and catalog/tools.json. The folder step makes ~/Projects/<name> unless the starting folder is already a project, and never moves files.

Already decided: when unsure, hand off, never guess (an unexpected exit code, a step far past its expected time). Every step checks before it acts. Library plus thin CLI.

Seams: reuse internal/detect, internal/screen, internal/session and the clt and brew watchers behind `wait clt` and `wait brew`. The server (internal/server) gains a way to run the flow; keep its existing page, token and lifetime rules.

Out of scope: the CLI verbs (next leaf) and the real installers (the installer leaf); use the fake Runner here.

Risks: the session log's format is shared by the CLI, the server and the page. Change it in one place, with one struct both sides import.

data.title: Add the run, wait and resume verbs
data.description:
Why: these are the agent's whole interface to the server-driven flow. A weak model must be able to drive it by following each output's `next:` line alone.

What: `bootstrap run --agent <app>` starts the server and the flow, detached, and returns at once with `next: bootstrap wait`; a second `run` joins the flow already running. `bootstrap wait` blocks until the flow needs the agent, or its budget runs out (exit 3, "still working, run wait again"), and either way prints the events since the last wait as rows written to be retold. `bootstrap resume --retry|--skip` hands back after a handoff. `stop`, `status` and the read verbs stay. Examples of the rows and of a handoff are in project/2026-11-05-server-driven-flow.md, "The shape".

Already decided: the house CLI rules in project/agents/cli-design.md: terse rows with `--json` on request, the shared exit codes, a bare `bootstrap` as a primer, every error and ack naming the next command, and tests that drive the binary and read the remedy. Keep wait's default budget under Claude Code's 10-minute tool limit, and check OpenCode's.

Seams: internal/cli; `show` and `wait answer|clt|brew` stay for the handoff screens, tests and the preview. Out of scope: SETUP.md.

Open, the agent's call: exact flag names, and whether `run` replaces `serve` or wraps it.

criteria.label: Tests drive the binary through run, wait (events and a budget timeout), a handoff, resume --retry and resume --skip, asserting output and exit codes
Every handoff type has a test that reads its remedy

data.title: Wire the real installers
data.description:
Why: the core runs on a fake Runner; this leaf makes each step act on a real Mac.

What: each step's check and act for real, called by full path (/opt/homebrew/bin/brew, never `brew` by name, because a running session can't find it after the .pkg installs): Apple's tools (about 20 GB free first, `xcode-select --install`, raise the window with `open -a`, the clt signals); Homebrew (find the latest .pkg, check it's signed by 927JGANW46 and notarized, open it, wait for brew); `brew trust bensyverson/tap` before installing the picked tools; Git (repo, .gitignore, first commit); GitHub (`github.com/signup` when the person has no account, then `gh auth login --web`, with the one-time code shown on the page, and `gh auth status`); the project (`agents init`, `agents migrate` when init asks, local/ and its .gitignore entry, `job init --as <agent>` unless .jobs.db exists, `job gitignore`); machine settings through each tool's own `hook install` (GGbVZ5, blocked on those tools shipping it).

The spike decides which of these run detached and which become handoffs; follow its findings, and edit this description if they change the premise.

Seams: internal/flow's Runner. New screens for GitHub (signup, the one-time code) go through internal/screen, with words for Ben to approve; 6jPdjy owns the remaining screens and real cards.

data.title: Wake the flow at once when the server records an answer
data.description:
Why: Ben asked, 2026-11-05, "Why are we polling rather than just sending events to the server?" The flow (internal/flow, run.poll) re-reads the session log every 200 ms (defaultPoll) to notice the person's answer. But the answer arrives as a POST to the server, which appends it to the log in the same process the flow runs in, so the poll adds up to 200 ms after every click for no reason. The click is the moment the page must feel instant (Ben: "hopefully that's not a long delay, since we own that transition").

What: when the server appends anything to the log itself (an answer, a tab change), the flow wakes at once, through an in-process signal. Writes from other processes (the agent's `bootstrap resume`, `show`, `stop`) still reach the flow by reading the log, either by a slower poll or by watching the file with kqueue through the standard library's syscall package (no new dependency). Those aren't latency-sensitive, since no person is waiting on a button. The log stays the single source of truth: the signal only says "look now", and the flow still reads the state from the log.

Seams: internal/server (where answers are appended, and Config.Flow), internal/flow (run.poll, Config.Poll), internal/session (Store). Keep the CLI stateless: commands never talk to the server.

Out of scope: the page's own stream (server-sent events), unless the same signal makes its tail cheaper too; say so if it does.

data.title: Live with, or head off, the agent's early git clone
data.description:
Third clean-Mac run, 2026-11-06 (project/2026-11-06-clean-mac-trial-findings.md, "Third run", finding 1). Given only the bare link, Claude Code on Opus 5.5 tried `gh repo view` and then `git clone` before reading anything. On a clean Mac, Apple's stand-in git opens the "install the command line developer tools?" dialog about a minute before the setup asks for it. The README's "curl the raw file, not gh/git" can't help, because the agent acts before reading it. It did no harm this time: Install on either dialog installs the same tools.

Options to weigh: put a line for agents in the repo's GitHub "About" description, which `gh repo view` and a fetch of the page show early; make Apple's step say plainly that a dialog may already be open and is the same one; or accept it. What would make it matter: a person who cancels the early dialog and then can't find Apple's step's window, or a trial where the two dialogs fight.

criteria.label: A trial where the agent clones first still reaches Apple's step with one dialog the person can find
